_note: Board 52:2 is the MASTER assembled shell — the whole editor at 1440 with the
drawer pinned — and almost every part of it is already conformed by another
recipe. What is genuinely THIS board's is the ARRANGEMENT (the pinned drawer's
own column) and THE RAIL: `s1-1-coach-dismissed` defers the rail items to here
in as many words ("the Rail family (52:2 / 199:2) owns those"), and until now
the owning board had no recipe, so the rail had never been measured against
anything.
The state is reached the way a person reaches it — boot, dismiss the first-run
coach if it is up, press the Layers rail tab, which is the tab the board draws
active with its panel in the pinned drawer.
WHAT MOVED:
2034:8415 + 5 siblings — every rail item is `--radius/md` (6). `.ls-btn` had
a hardcoded `border-radius: 7px`, one pixel off the token, on all six.
2034:8421 — the active bar is `rounded-[2px]`. It shipped `rounded-r-[2px]`,
so its two left corners were square. The code comment beside it cites board
199:2, and correctly — but 199:2 settles the bar's POSITION (3px, flush to
the rail edge, the item's full 44) and says nothing about corners, which is
what 52:2 draws. Position, size and fill were already right and still are.
52:7 — the drawer's edge now declares its colour on all four sides
(`border: 0 solid var(--bk-gray-100)` + `border-right-width: 1px`) instead of
the one-sided `border-right` shorthand. Identical pixels: a one-sided
shorthand leaves the other three sides at `currentColor`, so what any reader
— this harness included — got back for `border-top-color` was `--bk-ink`
#111827, not the token the rule names. `.bdi-panel` already documents this
exact pattern for the inspector's edge and calls it out as "what the recipes
read back"; the drawer had simply never been converted.

slots, and `rail-active-bar` on the active item's rule. None on
AquibraStudio.tsx, which this arc may not stage.
